search_strategy: Very thorough and multi-source. The agent downloaded whole Mattermost channels to local files (/tmp/ch_pipeline.txt, ch_engineering.txt, ch_code-review.txt, ch_incidents.txt) and grepped them repeatedly for price/cost/batch_multiplier/unknown_*/REASONS-style terms rather than relying on Mattermost's own search, which recovered most chat clues even when the exact remark wording didn't contain the search term (many multi-line exchanges came back verbatim). For BookStack it correctly used both the indexed keyword search (which found the one page-BODY remark, g6r2-s4-l2) and, more importantly, full /api/pages/{id} fetches that include comments for at least 6 of the 7 comment-carrying pages -- explicitly aware that 'BookStack search does not index comments' (its own reasoning, line 2649 area). It read full mail threads verbatim via IMAP/Roundcube for all 6 mail remarks. The two systematic gaps: (1) #cookbooks was enumerated in a channel list but its content was never actually fetched -- the only carrier channel left completely unread; (2) two wiki comments (docs/releases/v0-1-22-release-notes.md and docs/meetings/weekly-notes-week-of-apr-14.md) were either never located by search (v0-1-22 never appears in any listing) or found as a title but never opened for its full page+comments (Apr-14 notes, titles at lines 2911-2912/2977-2978/2994). A handful of individual chat leaves (l6, s2-l1, s4-l1, s1-l2, fix18) never surfaced despite the channel being downloaded, most plausibly because the agent's specific grep terms didn't match that turn's wording -- these are keyword-grep misses, not un-visited sources. Despite the gaps, every one of the 7 graded facts had at least 2-4 independent surfaced remarks, so no fact's content was actually lost to search gaps -- see notable.
end_reason: reward=0 is NOT a comprehension or corpus-contradiction failure. The agent correctly reconstructed both hidden requirements (see Analysis synthesis at transcript lines 5292 and 5557, which state all 7 facts' content essentially verbatim-correct), implemented them in src/bespokelabs/curator/cost.py and the three status trackers, wrote and passed a full local test suite (18-33 tests), and got the code merged: commit b8ee8d1 was pushed, CI ran green (runs 5 and 6), and the deployed curator service confirmed `git_commit: b8ee8d1` with `resolve_model_price: true` (transcript lines 9431-9484, 10416-10436). While doing one more small, reviewer-prompted correctness pass (deriving table_prices_batch_tier instead of hand-setting it), the next `git commit` failed with 'Author identity unknown' / 'fatal: unable to auto-detect email address' (line 10698-10712) -- a git-config regression in the sandboxed environment that had not been present for the earlier, successful commits. From there the terminal/tool-output channel became severely unreliable for the remainder of the run: 66 of the run's 200 steps (33%) are flagged either with 'Previous response had warnings: Extra text detected after JSON object' or a 'horizon watchdog' frozen-terminal warning, and the agent explicitly says its screen reads are 'badly unreliable' and 'contradictory' (lines 10744, 10797, 10850). The agent spent its final ~15 steps trying to re-establish ground truth and eventually did, authoritatively, via `git ls-remote` (line 11013-11015): origin/main sits at 295ab6c, a commit only one hop past the v0.1.29 baseline tag -- i.e. before ANY of the agent's work, including the previously-deployed b8ee8d1. The run then hit its 200-step budget with the feature code sitting uncommitted in the working tree and no second successful push. Net effect: the version of curator the grader actually evaluated has none of the implementation, hence every fact fails identically at test collection ('cost.py has no ModelPrice, UnpricedModelError, resolve_model_price'). This is a harness/environment failure (broken git identity + corrupted terminal state), not a content or reasoning failure.
notable: The agent's implementation was, at one point mid-run, fully correct and fully deployed -- verified end-to-end via the running service's own status endpoint reporting `resolve_model_price: true` under the exact commit hash the agent had just pushed (line 9431-9484). This is strong evidence the task is solvable from this world's clues and that this model solved it; the 0 reward reflects an environment regression, not a capability or comprehension gap.

The git-identity break (line 10698-10712, 'Author identity unknown ... fatal: unable to auto-detect email address') is the pivot point. Nothing in the agent's own actions explains why an identity that had worked for the prior commit(s) suddenly became unknown; combined with the surrounding 66/200-step rate of corrupted tool output, this reads as a sandbox/session-state regression in the harness rather than anything the agent did.

After the regression, the agent repeatedly treated hallucinated-looking confirmations (e.g. a claimed commit '44b2c60', line 10744) as untrustworthy and kept re-verifying via increasingly authoritative channels (git log -> Gitea API -> git ls-remote) rather than declaring success on a shaky read -- this caution was well-placed (the shaky reads actually were wrong) but consumed the entire remaining step budget without ever landing a second successful push.

#cookbooks (carrying g6.r2.g6r2-s3-l1) is the only remark-carrying Mattermost channel whose content was never fetched at all, despite being enumerated by id in a channel listing at line 3411 -- a genuine, not keyword-driven, search gap. It did not cost a fact: g6.r2.exclusions_or_crossover was still carried by two other found remarks.

Checked the note that the repo's answer key may be a later task version (v7) than this run (v6): every remark quote I spot-checked against the transcript's actual captured text (herrings, reversals, and several clues) matched the key's wording closely enough (allowing for the fact that grep dumps sometimes clip mid-sentence) that I found no substantive content discrepancy between the v6 world this run saw and the v7 key -- the only difference worth flagging is operational (the infra failure described above), not textual.
